questions.question: According to Figure 8.2, which development stage is most appropriate for applying software inspections as part of verification and validation?
questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Understand | Difficulty: Medium] Figure 8.2 indicates that software inspections support V&V at the design stage, where they can catch defects before coding begins. [Page 38]

questions.question: Why might a critical‑system project establish a separate testing group within the development team?

options.A: To reduce the total number of tests needed
options.B: To allow developers to write code faster
options.C: To ensure tests are developed and results are recorded independently of implementation
options.D: To eliminate the need for unit testing altogether

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Understand | Difficulty: Easy] The text states that a separate testing group is responsible for developing tests and maintaining detailed records, providing a formal, independent testing process for critical systems. [Page 41]

---

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the primary focus of unit testing?

options.A: Verifying the entire system meets user requirements
options.B: Testing individual program components such as methods or classes
options.C: Evaluating the performance of the software under load
options.D: Checking that the software documentation is complete

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Remember | Difficulty: Easy] Unit testing is defined as testing program components like methods or object classes. [Page 41]

questions.question: When designing unit‑test cases, the text recommends using approaches from which section?
questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Remember | Difficulty: Easy] The passage explicitly refers to using the test‑case design approaches discussed in Section 8.1.2 for unit tests. [Page 41]

questions.question: Which statement best captures the relationship between verification and validation as described in the material?

options.A: Verification checks that the software does what the user wants; validation checks that it meets the specification.
options.B: Verification and validation are the same activity performed at different times.
options.C: Verification ensures the software meets its specification; validation ensures it delivers the functionality expected by the customer.
options.D: Validation is performed only after the software is released, while verification is done during coding.

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Understand | Difficulty: Medium] The text defines verification as checking conformance to specifications and validation as confirming delivery of expected functionality. [Page 37]

questions.question: According to the provided context, at what point do verification and validation activities begin in a software project?

options.A: After the coding phase is complete
options.B: Only during the system testing stage
options.C: As soon as requirements become available and continue through all stages
options.D: Only after user acceptance testing is finished

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Remember | Difficulty: Easy] The passage states that V&V processes start when requirements are available and continue throughout development. [Page 37]

questions.question: Which of the following is *not* one of the three stages of development testing mentioned in the excerpt?
questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Remember | Difficulty: Easy] The three stages listed are unit, integration, and system testing; acceptance testing is not included. [Page 41]

questions.question: How does the text suggest test inputs should be varied when performing unit testing?

options.A: By using only the maximum and minimum possible values
options.B: By calling the routine with different input parameters to explore behavior
options.C: By running the routine once with a default configuration
options.D: By automating tests without considering input diversity

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Understand | Difficulty: Medium] Unit testing involves calling methods with varied inputs to assess different execution paths. [Page 41]

questions.question: Dijkstra’s “The Humble Programmer” is cited in the context. Which underlying principle from that citation aligns with the need for thorough testing?

options.A: Programmers should write as much code as possible quickly.
options.B: Simplicity and humility in programming reduce the likelihood of defects, supporting the case for systematic testing.
options.C: Testing is unnecessary if the code is well‑documented.
options.D: Only senior programmers need to be concerned with testing.

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Understand | Difficulty: Medium] Dijkstra’s essay advocates modest, disciplined coding, which logically leads to the importance of careful testing. [Page 36]

questions.question: What is the main benefit of maintaining detailed records of test results, as emphasized for critical systems?

options.A: It allows developers to skip future testing phases.
options.B: It provides evidence of compliance and facilitates defect tracking and audit.
options.C: It reduces the time needed for code reviews.
options.D: It eliminates the need for unit testing.

questions.explanation: [Bloom: Understand | Difficulty: Easy] The passage notes that the separate testing group maintains detailed test records, which support accountability and traceability in critical systems. [Page 41]
